solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In France I must keep a horse, it being for James

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the French word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: je is the French word for I
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman insists on owning a horse because it is meant for someone called James.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jacobite backed the exiled Stuart King James II and his heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the deposed Stuart king James were called by a name formed from Jacobus, Latin for James.

definitions.meaning: the ... were a Germanic people who settled in Kent in the fifth century
coarse fibre woven into sacks and hessian

explanation.surface: A query whether a pioneer from long ago was dismissed from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' looks like dismissal; it is the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both an early Germanic people and the plant fibre used for coarse sackcloth.

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw
a wag is a joker

explanation.surface: Punch, the puppet, is a comedian who keeps talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for a long friendly chat or gossip session.

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
a Green is an environmentalist; the 's stands for 'is', joining the pieces to the definition

explanation.surface: A bold campaigner for the planet strikes a certain note in speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tone' suggests a manner of speaking; here it means a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark green shade like the glass of wine bottles is one colour tone.

definitions.meaning: a horse expected to win has been recommended by tipsters

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both knocked over and recommended as a likely winner by racing pundits.

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
a hat is worn on the head

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a broad-brimmed hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An interrogative word used on its own as a question asking for something to be repeated.

indicators.note: the numeral sits within the word for a crowd

parts.note: a host is a great number, a multitude
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is raised up among a throng, as at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for raising something up, especially with effort or by rope.

clue.text: Poet's sonnet composed about New York

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the city's abbreviation
composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of sonnet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet writes a sonnet on the subject of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but means around: the rearranged letters TENSON, from 'composed', go around the city's initials. The 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Victorian Poet Laureate, author of In Memoriam.

indicators.note: the article is placed within the word for colour

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An instruction to mark a piece of writing in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain or blemish, a trace of something bad, is a mark on something.

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, a mess, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A marksman uses terrible words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful language' looks like swearing; 'awful' is the anagram signal. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Persian, or Farsi, is the main tongue spoken in Iran.

clue.text: One let off a wicked thing in the Vatican?

definitions.meaning: something set off or fired, like a firework

definitions.text: a wicked thing in the Vatican?
definitions.meaning: a candle has a wick, and the Vatican is in Rome

explanation.definitionFit: A firework tube shooting out balls of light, whose name also describes a wax candle in Rome.

clue.text: Fantasist, amusing, about to modify dream finally

indicators.note: the word for amusing goes about, or around, the other pieces

parts.note: witty means amusing and clever
to alter is to modify

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of dream

explanation.surface: A daydreamer, entertaining, is ready to change a dream at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is the daydreaming hero of a James Thurber story.
explanation.definitionFit: The name has become a byword for an ordinary person who lives in heroic daydreams.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Complainers annoy a music writer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin was the American who wrote Rhapsody in Blue and Porgy and Bess.

parts.note: en is French for in
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Enlist Frenchmen at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in good time' reads as 'promptly', but 'in' belongs with 'French'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for taking someone on, as an employee or soldier.

indicators.note: in says the name lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: A Spaniard might be part of a gang running away to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name found in Spain and Italy, so a Spaniard may bear it; the maybe marks an example.

clue.text: English like to look after part of London

parts.note: as means like, in the sense 'as good as'
to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: An English person is fond of caring for a corner of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' looks like a verb of fondness; it is AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The district east of the City, home of Cockneys, is a region of the capital.

clue.text: Man leading two ducks and a penguin

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the word for man comes first

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O; two of them are OO

explanation.surface: A fellow walks ahead of a pair of ducks and a penguin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentoo is a species of penguin with a white stripe across its head.

clue.text: Pets from Asia, etc, mess all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Animals from Asia and elsewhere make a mess everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Siamese cats are a popular breed of household animal, as companions.

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A suitable girl is matched with her previous partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective 'suitable'; it is the verb, to take over.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for seizing territory or property and taking it for oneself.

clue.text: First of the regulars, usually extremely faithful

indicators.note: First of takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The leading regular customers are, most often, extremely loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal and steadfast; a true friend is a faithful one.

clue.text: It's used to fasten head on fly

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means the head word follows the fly word

parts.note: to wing is to fly
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: Something for attaching a head to an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded fastener with two flat projections so it can be turned by hand onto a bolt.

parts.note: to rear a child is to bring it up

explanation.surface: Raising a daughter is a gloomy business.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary synonym for dull, cheerless and gloomy.

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for catch goes around the numeral

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Someone will catch about ten fish later.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means afterwards, coming in the following place.

parts.note: a skeleton is made of bones, and an inactive workforce is idle

explanation.definitionFit: Utterly lazy, idle to the very core, playfully pictured as a skeleton crew doing nothing.
